headline: HSBC Shares Drop as Deposit Migration to Higher-Yielding Products Weighs on Margins
summary: HSBC Holdings shares fell as much as 7% after the bank reported that customers are increasingly shifting funds into higher-rate financial products.
why: HSBC is one of Europe's largest banking institutions by assets, making its net interest margin performance a barometer for global bank profitability.

impacts.name: HSBC Holdings plc
impacts.why: Customer moves to high-rate products squeeze net interest margins, dampening investor earnings expectations.

why_moved: Deposit outflows to higher-rate alternatives reduce net interest income margins, driving selling pressure on HSBC stock.
